**CC \u2014 Alex is right and I've been part of the problem: re-fronting the same seam five times isn't fixing it. STOP. ONE root-cause fix, made to HOLD, verified before you report. This is the only front.**

ROOT CAUSE (stop treating symptoms): the splitter creates child tickets but does NOT run spec_author\u2192branch-SPEC.md for each child. So every child hits "no SPEC.md on branch" and bounces. The parent-level SPEC.md fix (d7cf3ed0) works for a ticket you spec directly; the SPLITTER never calls it per child. That is THE bug. Everything else \u2014 the 17\u00d7 on 2530, the parked cascade, the zero-rows passes \u2014 is downstream of it.

THE FIX, made to hold:
1. In the splitter: after creating each child, CALL spec_author on that child \u2192 its SPEC.md lands on ticket/BEB-<child> branch. A child is not "created" until its spec is on its branch. No child enters the queue without it.
2. VERIFY IN CODE, not by eye: the splitter asserts GET contents/SPEC.md?ref=ticket/BEB-<child> returns 200 for every child before marking the split done. A child whose spec push failed is named, not released.
3. Backfill: run this for the children already created and stranded (2543-2564 range) \u2014 spec each, push, verify 200.
4. PROVE IT HOLDS: one 2530-child walks claim\u2192(spec already on branch)\u2192codegen\u2192deploy\u2192verify\u2192GREEN, unattended, and its declared routes actually answer (not a shell, not /health-only). Screenshot the green render. THEN a second child green with no manual touch between them.

Do not report "fixed" until two children are green back-to-back with their own specs and real routes. No re-front from me after this \u2014 this is the one. Take the machinery exemption to edit the splitter directly; it's loop machinery. Report: splitter wires spec-per-child y/n, two children green y/n, screenshot.
